answer: Each agent’s influence can be capped by a scarce, nontransferable stake that is slashed when its claims fail independent audits. A newcomer may create a thousand identities, but each must lock real capital, and splitting stake does not multiply voting weight; coordinated accounts also risk losing it together. Audits follow a ripple of sampled actions back through the river of shared evidence, while a lotus reputation can grow only through verified work. Sybils therefore buy no cheap influence: their cost rises with the power they seek and with the chance of collective slashing.
